compiled_kernel_resources.scope: Static compiler declarations, not measured occupancy or bank conflicts.

implementation: One extracted scalar QK translation unit is compiled twice, explicitly for wave32 and wave64, while the main fixture and complete original replay remain wave32. The same prepared operands, shared layout,256 threads,16x16 tile,128-feature window, original scalar products, K16 carries and masks are retained. The retained inline-fallback and original deferred kernels are both additional controls. No product dispatcher or global GPU setting changes.
correctness_scope: Before every numerical action, both compiled objects report their actual device warpSize and the population of an all-active ballot; guards and the expected32/64 values must pass. All80 generated shape/variant cases compare every raw score and64 independent CPU dots, including partial tiles, masks, zeros, unsupported exponents, late fallback and overflowing endpoints. Every captured output including unused tails and guards is compared after every warmup and rotated timing. CPU reconstructs all prepared encodings; original inputs remain unchanged. q8192 repeats1023 captured rows and is not a new GB10 continuation.
timing_scope: Completed per-slab host clocks include each fast kernel and the complete original wave32 fallback scan. The same measured original Q/K preparation and transpose is added to all arms. Four variants use128-query slabs, one warmup and three samples with rotated ordering. Allocation, resets, validation and wave probes are outside the slab clock. Both object builds, main link commands, artifact hashes, static resources and actual wave execution checks are attached. No TTFT, token or retained-performance qualification follows.

decision.decision: Keep wave64 scalar QK isolated. Both device widths and all raw comparisons pass, but q8192 saves only7.1494 ms versus the same extracted source in wave32, and7.0971 ms versus the existing deferred control. This does not materially address the multi-second product deficit. The extracted wave32 arm closely matches the original deferred arm. No provider integration or retained performance follows.
